generic_name: Insulin Syringe with Needle, 0.3 mL (Half-Unit Markings)
purpose: This is a small syringe used to inject insulin for managing blood sugar in people with diabetes. The 0.3 mL size is designed for people who take smaller doses of insulin. The half-unit markings make it easier to measure very precise, small doses accurately.
how_it_works: You draw insulin from a vial into this syringe and inject it under your skin, usually in your abdomen, thigh, or upper arm. The tiny needle is designed to be as comfortable as possible. The half-unit markings (like 0.5, 1.5, 2.5 units) help you measure doses more precisely than a standard syringe, which is especially important for children or people on very low insulin doses.
common_side_effects: Minor pain, redness, or a small bruise at the injection site are common. Rotating your injection sites helps reduce skin irritation or hard lumps (lipodystrophy) from repeated injections in the same spot.
warnings: Never reuse syringes — they can become dull and increase infection risk. Always dispose of used syringes safely in an approved sharps container. Keep syringes away from children. Make sure you are using the correct syringe for your insulin concentration (most insulins are U-100). Double-check your dose carefully before injecting.
typical_dosing: Use as directed by your doctor or diabetes care team. This syringe holds up to 0.3 mL (30 units of U-100 insulin). The half-unit markings allow doses as small as 0.5 units. Always match the syringe to your prescribed insulin dose and concentration.
